title: Macelignan mitigates oxidative and inflammatory damage in hypoxic neurons through PPARgamma-dependent pathways: implications for Alzheimer's disease.
authors: Chu, Xinge; Qi, Zhengyu; Li, Sha; Qiu, Xinru; Yan, Guanghai; Cui, Chunai
one_liner_zh: 研究天然化合物Macelignan通过PPARgamma通路缓解缺氧神经元损伤，仅用分子对接初步识别靶点，未涉及蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Oxidative injury under hypoxic conditions constitutes an important pathological factor in the progression of neuronal loss in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Macelignan, a natural lignan from Myristica fragrans, possesses antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, yet its neuroprotective mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we aimed to elucidate the molecular targets and signaling pathways by which macelignan protects neurons from hypoxia-induced oxidative damage. Neuronal damage was modeled in vitro in HT22 murine hippocampal neurons using cobalt (II) chloride (CoCl2) or conditioned medium from CoCl2-activated BV2 microglia, and in vivo in Wistar rats subjected to bilateral common carotid artery occlusion (BCCAo) to mimic hypoxic injury. We found that macelignan significantly improved neuronal viability, attenuated apoptosis, reduced intracellular and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, and preserved mitochondrial membrane potential(DeltaPsim). Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-gamma (PPARgamma), a ligand-activated transcription factor regulating oxidative metabolism and limiting neuroinflammation, was identified via molecular docking as a potential target of macelignan. Functional assays demonstrated that macelignan acts as a PPARgamma agonist, activating the Nrf2/HO-1 antioxidant pathway and suppressing NF-kappaB-mediated inflammation. These effects were diminished by the PPARgamma antagonist GW9662. In BV2 microglia, macelignan modulated polarization toward anti-inflammatory phenotypes, reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine release, and mitigated secondary neuronal injury in HT22 cells. In BCCAo rats, macelignan alleviated hippocampal pathology and improved spatial and recognition memory. In summary, macelignan mitigates hypoxia-induced neuronal injury by targeting PPARgamma, leading to coordinated activation of antioxidant defenses and suppression of neuroinflammation. These results provide new insight into the therapeutic potential of macelignan for hypoxia-associated AD.
abstract_zh: 缺氧条件下的氧化损伤是阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer's disease, AD）神经元丢失进展中的重要病理因素。Macelignan，一种来自肉豆蔻（Myristica fragrans）的天然木脂素，具有抗氧化和抗炎活性，但其神经保护机制尚不清楚。在本研究中，我们旨在阐明macelignan保护神经元免受缺氧诱导氧化损伤的分子靶点和信号通路。使用氯化钴（cobalt (II) chloride, CoCl2）或CoCl2激活的BV2小胶质细胞条件培养基，在体外HT22小鼠海马神经元中模拟神经元损伤，并在体内通过双侧颈总动脉闭塞（bilateral common carotid artery occlusion, BCCAo）的大鼠中模拟缺氧损伤。我们发现，macelignan显著提高神经元活力、减轻凋亡、降低细胞内和线粒体活性氧（reactive oxygen species, ROS）水平，并维持线粒体膜电位（DeltaPsim）。过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体-γ（Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-gamma, PPARgamma），一种调节氧化代谢并限制神经炎症的配体激活转录因子，通过分子对接被鉴定为macelignan的潜在靶点。功能实验表明，macelignan作为PPARgamma激动剂，激活Nrf2/HO-1抗氧化通路并抑制NF-kappaB介导的炎症。这些效应被PPARgamma拮抗剂GW9662减弱。在BV2小胶质细胞中，macelignan调节向抗炎表型的极化，减少促炎细胞因子释放，并减轻HT22细胞中的继发性神经元损伤。在BCCAo大鼠中，macelignan减轻海马病理并改善空间和识别记忆。总之，macelignan通过靶向PPARgamma减轻缺氧诱导的神经元损伤，导致抗氧化防御的协调激活和神经炎症的抑制。这些结果为macelignan在缺氧相关AD中的治疗潜力提供了新见解。
